claims.text: Pack cementation with aluminum oxide can improve the high-temperature oxygen resistance of refractory high-entropy alloys.
The pack-cementation treatment will produce an aluminum oxide layer on the alloy surface.
The resulting aluminum oxide layer will be dense and continuous.
A dense, continuous aluminum oxide layer acts as a barrier to oxygen diffusion.
Restricting oxygen diffusion through the aluminum oxide layer reduces the alloy's oxidation rate.
At 1000°C in air for 100 hours, the treated alloy will have an oxidation rate at least 50% lower than the untreated alloy.
The proposed intervention is expected to work over 900–1100°C in oxidizing environments.
Alloy composition and microstructure may influence oxidation behavior and treatment effectiveness.

contradictions.description: The prediction requires at least a 50% oxidation-rate reduction, whereas the falsification rule only rejects the hypothesis when the treated alloy is not significantly better. A statistically significant reduction smaller than 50% would violate the quantified prediction without satisfying the stated falsification rule.
